Yes! I read it last month. I'd rather read the book than watch the film.
Really? Why?
When I read, I use my imagination. I can see the main character in my own way.

p2.t: I prefer films to books. I get bored when there are no pictures.
Then you should try comics! They have stories and pictures.
Good idea. But tell me, does this story have a happy ending?

Very! It's cool and clean, and the trains have no drivers.

It's easy. You can pay with a card at the station.

I don't mind the farm. It's cheaper, and it's outdoors.

p1.t: Noura, you look tired. What happened last night?
Well, I was doing my homework when the doorbell rang.
Who was it?
My aunt and her five children! It was a big surprise. They arrived from Hail without calling.

p2.t: Oh no! Was your house ready for guests?
Not at all! The living room was in a mess, and my brothers were playing video games.
What did you do?
We got ready very quickly. Mum made coffee, and I tidied the room.
And did you finish your homework?
No, I didn't! We were talking until midnight.

p1.t: Emma, did you enjoy the picnic on Friday?
It was a disaster! We were having lunch in the park when suddenly it started to rain.
Did you get wet?
Very wet! It was raining heavily, and our picnic things were in a mess.

p2.t: Was there thunder and lightning too?
Yes, lots! My little sister was crying, and Dad was looking for the car keys.
Oh no. What happened when you got home?
While we were changing our clothes, there was a power cut! We sat in the dark for an hour.
What a day! But I still love the rain.

Oh no! What were you doing?
I was riding down a hill when suddenly my wheel slipped on some wet sand.

p2.t: Did you hurt yourself badly?
Not really, but my knee was bleeding. A man ran over and asked, 'Are you OK?'
That was kind. Did he help you?
Yes. He had a first aid kit, so he cleaned my knee and put a plaster on it.
You were lucky.
I know! Next time I'll ride more slowly.

At the café. I was looking for my money when I saw that my purse wasn't in my bag.

p2.t: Were you worried?
Very! We went back to the shoe shop, but it wasn't there.
So what did you do?
We asked a security guard. Luckily, a woman found my purse and took it to the information desk.

Yes! He was playing an old king, and he was sitting on a big, comfortable chair.

Nothing! Everyone thought it was a joke. Then Khalid woke up and said the wrong line by mistake.
Was he embarrassed?
At first, yes. But then he laughed too, and everyone clapped.

dialogue.scene: Lama asks her grandfather, Grandpa Saleh, to tell her a story from when he was a boy.

p1.t: Grandpa, tell me a story from when you were young.
All right. One day, when I was twelve, I was looking after our camels in the desert.
Alone?
Yes. At first, everything was fine. I was sitting under a tree when suddenly a sandstorm started.

p2.t: What did you do?
I couldn't see anything, and I got lost. I walked for hours.
Were you scared?
Very! Luckily, the camels knew the way home, so I followed them.
And in the end?
In the end, I got home at night. My mother was crying, but she was so happy to see me.

prompts.q: It's a new white ball. What will you do after the match?
prompts.hint: Promise what you will do with the ball: 'I'll …'.

prompts.q: When will you give it back?
prompts.hint: Say a time, and make a promise with 'I won't …' too.

culture.title: Keeping Promises
points: An Arabic saying tells us that a promise is like a debt: you must keep it.
In Japan and the USA, children sometimes make a 'pinky promise' by holding their little fingers together.
In many cultures, people shake hands when they agree to do something.
qs: Why is it important to keep a promise?
Have you ever made a promise that was hard to keep?

3-2.exit: Make two promises to me: one with 'I'll' and one with 'I won't'.

3-3.objective: Today you will predict what your life might be like when you grow up.
3-3.warmup: What did you want to be when you were younger?

expressions.def: to become an adult
expressions.frame: When I grow up, I'll probably ___.

expressions.def: to start to be something
expressions.frame: I might become a ___ one day.

expressions.def: a person who designs machines, roads or buildings
expressions.frame: An engineer can build ___.

expressions.def: a place where people study after they finish school
expressions.frame: I'd like to study ___ at university.

expressions.def: something you really want to do one day
expressions.frame: My dream is to ___.

expressions.def: a person who plans and makes video games
expressions.frame: A game designer needs to be good at ___.

dialogue.scene: It's careers day at school. Reem and her friend Sara are talking about their future.

p1.t: Reem, what do you want to be when you grow up?
My dream is to become an engineer. I love building things.
Cool! Will you study at university here?
Probably. I'll study in Riyadh, and I might go abroad for a year too.

p2.t: What about you, Sara?
I'm not sure yet. I might become a game designer, or I might be a teacher.
A game designer? That's a great job! Will you make games for children?
Definitely! And I'll put a character called Reem in my first game.
Ha! I promise I'll play it every day.

dialogue.focus: I might become a game designer, or I might be a teacher.
qs: What does Reem want to become?
What will Sara put in her first game?

speakout.scene: I'm a reporter for a TV show called 'Kids of Today'. I'm asking children about their future.

prompts.q: What do you think you'll do when you grow up?
prompts.hint: Use 'I'll probably …' or 'I might …'.

prompts.q: Will you go to university? What will you study?
prompts.hint: Say how sure you are and name a subject.

prompts.q: Where do you think you'll live?
prompts.hint: Name a place and give a reason.

culture.title: New Jobs in Saudi Arabia
points: Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 plan aims to create many new jobs for young people.
There are now more jobs in tourism, technology, entertainment and sport.
Some jobs of the future don't exist yet, so children will need to learn new skills.
qs: Which job do you think will be popular in 2040?
Would you rather work in an office or outdoors? Why?

3-3.exit: Tell me two things you think you'll do when you grow up and one thing you might do.

3-4.objective: Today you will offer help to a friend and make promises to support them.
3-4.warmup: Who helps you when you have a problem?

expressions.def: words to tell someone not to feel bad or afraid
expressions.frame: Don't worry, I'll help you with ___.

expressions.def: to be sure that someone will help you
expressions.frame: You can count on me to ___.

expressions.def: to give something to someone for a short time
expressions.frame: I'll lend you my ___.

expressions.def: to not tell other people something private
expressions.frame: I promise I'll keep your secret about ___.

expressions.def: to help someone understand something
expressions.frame: I'll explain ___ to you after school.

expressions.def: a little afraid before something important
expressions.frame: I feel nervous before ___.

dialogue.scene: Lina was ill last week. Her friend Huda sees that she looks worried at school.

p1.t: Lina, are you OK? You look worried.
I missed three maths lessons last week. The test is on Sunday, and I'm really nervous.
Don't worry. I'll explain the lessons to you at break.
Really? Thank you so much!

p2.t: I'll lend you my notebook too. All the lessons are in it.
That's very kind. I promise I'll give it back on Sunday after the test.
No problem. You can count on me.
One more thing. Please don't tell the others I'm nervous.
Of course. I'll keep your secret. I won't tell anyone.

dialogue.focus: Don't worry. I'll explain the lessons to you at break.
qs: Why is Lina nervous?
What will Huda lend Lina?

speakout.scene: I'm your friend. I've got a big swimming race on Saturday, and I'm very nervous. Help me!

prompts.q: I'm so nervous! What can you do to help me?
prompts.hint: Offer help with 'Don't worry, I'll …'.

prompts.q: Will you come and watch the race?
prompts.hint: Make a promise with 'I promise I'll …'.

prompts.q: I fell in the pool at the last race. Please don't tell anyone!
prompts.hint: Promise to keep the secret with 'I won't …'.

culture.title: Friends Help Friends
points: The United Nations has an International Day of Friendship on 30 July.
An Arabic saying tells us that a true friend is there for you when you have a problem.
In many schools around the world, older students help younger ones as 'buddies'.
qs: How do you help your friends when they have a problem?
What makes someone a good friend?

3-4.exit: Your friend is nervous about a test. Make two offers or promises to help.

3-5.objective: Today you will make predictions about our planet and promise what you will do to help it.
3-5.warmup: What do you do at home to help the planet?

expressions.def: the air, water and land around us
expressions.frame: One way to help the environment is ___.

expressions.def: to use paper, plastic or glass again to make new things
expressions.frame: At home, we recycle ___.

expressions.def: to use more of something than you need
expressions.frame: I won't waste ___ any more.

expressions.def: to put a young tree in the ground
expressions.frame: I'd like to plant a tree in ___.

expressions.def: to stop a machine or a light working
expressions.frame: I promise I'll turn off the ___ when I leave the room.

expressions.def: I'm telling you that I will really do this
expressions.frame: For the planet, I promise I'll ___.

dialogue.scene: Nasser and his sister Shahad are making a poster for their school's Green Week.

p1.t: Our school wants every student to make a green promise. What's yours, Nasser?
I promise I'll turn off the lights and the air conditioner when I leave my room.
Good one. I won't waste water when I brush my teeth.
Do you think the world will be hotter in the future?
Scientists think it probably will. And there might be less water.

p2.t: Then let's do more. Our family could recycle plastic bottles.
Yes! And I'll ask Dad if we can plant a tree in the garden.
Trees are great for the environment. They'll give us shade too.
Let's write our promises on the poster and put it on the fridge.

dialogue.focus: I promise I'll turn off the lights and the air conditioner when I leave my room.
qs: What does Shahad promise to do?
What does Shahad want to ask Dad?

speakout.scene: I'm the head of our school's Green Club. We're making a 'Green Promise Wall', and I'd like your predictions and your promise.

prompts.q: What do you think our planet will be like in 2050?
prompts.hint: Make a prediction with 'will', 'won't' or 'might'.

prompts.q: What will you promise to do for the environment?
prompts.hint: Make two promises with 'I promise I'll …' and 'I won't …'.

prompts.q: What can our school do?
prompts.hint: Suggest one idea and say what will happen.

culture.title: The Saudi Green Initiative
points: The Saudi Green Initiative started in 2021.
It plans to plant ten billion trees across Saudi Arabia in the coming years.
Trees give shade, clean the air and help to keep cities cooler.
qs: Where would you like to plant a tree in your city?
Do you think people will use less plastic in the future? Why?

3-5.exit: Make one prediction about our planet and one green promise.

words.ex: Have you ever tried Japanese food?
I've never tasted camel milk.
Taste the soup before you add salt.
This chicken is very spicy!
Kabsa is a famous Saudi dish.
I've been to that restaurant once.

dialogue.t: Have you ever tried jareesh, Sam?
No, I've never eaten it. What does it taste like?
It's soft and warm. Here, taste some.
Mmm, it's good! It isn't spicy at all.
Have you ever eaten anything really spicy?
Yes, I tried a very spicy curry once. My mouth was on fire!

grammar.title: Have you ever …? / I've never …
grammar.ar: نستخدم Have you ever + التصريف الثالث للفعل لنسأل عن تجربة في أي وقت من الحياة، ونستخدم I've never + التصريف الثالث لنقول إننا لم نفعلها أبداً.
examples: Have you ever tried sushi? Yes, I have.
I've never eaten camel meat.
She has tasted jareesh once.

words.ex: I've been to Jeddah three times.
My uncle often travels abroad for work.
The journey from Riyadh to Jeddah is very long by car.
We took photos of the view from the mountain.
Our first night in the desert was unforgettable.
Dad has gone to Dammam. He'll be back on Sunday.

dialogue.t: Where have you been, Reem?
I've been to Taif with my family.
I've never been there. Was it a long journey?
Yes, but the view from the mountains was amazing.
Have you ever travelled abroad?
Yes, I went to Malaysia two years ago. It was unforgettable!
Where's your brother?
He's gone to Jeddah with my uncle.

grammar.title: been to / gone to
grammar.ar: has been to = ذهب وعاد. has gone to = ذهب وما زال هناك. وعندما نذكر وقتاً محدداً نستخدم الماضي البسيط: I went there last year.
examples: I've been to Taif. I went there last week.
My brother has gone to Jeddah. He isn't here.
Have you ever been to Dammam?

words.ex: I've already packed my bag.
Have you finished your homework yet?
Dad has just arrived home.
I packed my torch and a warm jacket.
It was dark, so I used my torch.
Mum wrote a shopping list.

dialogue.t: Have you packed your bag yet, Omar?
Yes, I've already packed it. Here's my list.
Where's your torch?
Oh no! I haven't found it yet.
Have you charged the camera?
Yes, I've just charged it. It's ready.

grammar.title: already / yet / just
grammar.ar: already وjust تأتيان بين have/has والفعل: I've already eaten. أما yet فتأتي في آخر السؤال أو الجملة المنفية: Have you eaten yet? I haven't eaten yet.
examples: I've already done my homework.
Have you packed your bag yet?
She's just called me.

words.ex: We fed the ducks at the park.
Don't touch the cat. It's asleep.
Wild animals live in forests, deserts and seas.
My little brother is scared of dogs.
We stood close to the giraffe.
We saw a shark at the aquarium.

dialogue.t: We went to a camel farm. Have you ever fed a camel?
No, I've never been close to a camel.
I touched a baby camel too!
Cool! I've seen sharks at the aquarium.
Weren't you scared of them?
No, there was thick glass between us!

grammar.title: Present perfect: I've seen … / Have you ever fed …?
grammar.ar: نكوّن المضارع التام بـ have/has + التصريف الثالث. بعض الأفعال شاذة: see → seen، feed → fed، be → been، eat → eaten.
examples: I've seen a desert fox.
Have you ever fed a camel?
My sister has never touched a snake.

words.ex: I've learned how to make tea.
He practises swimming three times a week.
His English has improved a lot.
My parents are proud of me.
I swam in the sea for the first time last summer.
Don't give up! You can do it.

dialogue.t: You swim really well now, Khalid!
Thanks! I've learned how to swim on my back.
When did you start lessons?
Last October. I nearly gave up, but I practised a lot.
Your swimming has really improved!
Yes, and last week I swam in the sea for the first time.

grammar.title: Present perfect or past simple?
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع التام عندما لا نذكر وقتاً محدداً: I've learned to swim. وعندما نذكر الوقت (last year, in 2023, when I was six) نستخدم الماضي البسيط: I learned last year.
examples: I've learned how to cook rice.
I learned it last summer.
When did you start? I started in October.

words.ex: I had an interview with our school's football coach.
Have you ever been on a plane?
That was the best trip I've ever had.
You went to the match? How was it?
Camping in the desert was a great experience.
I've flown on a plane twice.

dialogue.t: Dana, have you ever won a prize?
Yes, I have. I've won two prizes for drawing.
When did you win your first prize?
In Grade 4. It was the best day I've ever had at school.
Have you ever been on a plane?
Yes, twice. I flew to Egypt last year.
How was it?
It was an amazing experience!

grammar.title: Asking about experiences: present perfect + past simple
grammar.ar: نبدأ بسؤال المضارع التام Have you ever …؟ وإذا كانت الإجابة نعم نسأل عن التفاصيل بالماضي البسيط: When did you …? How was it?
examples: Have you ever won a prize? Yes, I have.
When did you win it? I won it last year.
It's the best trip I've ever had.

words.ex: I prefer football to basketball.
My brother is really into chess.
We play outdoors when the weather is nice.
In summer, we usually play indoors.
Reading a book before bed is relaxing.
The long walk was tiring.

dialogue.t: Do you want to go cycling this afternoon?
I prefer swimming to cycling. Cycling is too tiring.
But it's outdoors, by the sea.
The pool is indoors, so it's cool.
What are you into these days?
I'm really into drawing. It's relaxing.

grammar.title: prefer … to …
grammar.ar: نستخدم prefer + اسم أو فعل بـ ing، ثم to + اسم أو فعل بـ ing. لا نستخدم than مع prefer.
examples: I prefer juice to milk.
I prefer swimming to cycling.
She prefers reading to watching TV.

words.ex: I'd rather have a burger than pizza.
I'd prefer orange juice, please.
Lunch is the biggest meal in our house.
Let's share a big pizza.
Grilled chicken is a healthy choice.
Fried potatoes are tasty but not very healthy.

dialogue.t: Let's get a burger meal.
I'd rather have something healthy.
Would you rather have a shawarma or a salad?
I'd prefer the salad, I think.
Do you want to share some fries?
Yes, but only a small portion!

grammar.title: I'd rather + verb / I'd prefer + noun
grammar.ar: بعد I'd rather نضع الفعل في صيغته الأساسية: I'd rather have water. وبعد I'd prefer نضع اسماً أو to + فعل: I'd prefer water. / I'd prefer to sit outside.
examples: I'd rather have a salad.
I'd prefer juice, please.
Would you rather have rice or bread?

words.ex: I'd rather stay in a hotel than in a tent.
We spent three days at the seaside.
We saw colourful fish when we went snorkelling.
Let's go for a walk and get some fresh air.
The beach was too crowded.
Which do you prefer, the sea or the mountains?

dialogue.t: Which do you prefer, the seaside or the mountains?
I'd rather go to the seaside. I want to go snorkelling.
But the beaches are crowded.
Not all of them. Some are very quiet.
I'd prefer to go to the mountains for the fresh air.
Let's ask Dad. Maybe we can do both!

grammar.title: would rather … than … / I'd prefer to …
grammar.ar: I'd rather + فعل أساسي + than + فعل أساسي (أو اسم). أما I'd prefer فيأتي بعده to + فعل.
examples: I'd rather go to the seaside than to the mountains.
I'd rather swim than walk.
I'd prefer to stay in a hotel.

words.ex: I read a comic about a superhero.
'Treasure Island' is a famous adventure story.
Reading helps your imagination grow.
The main character is a boy called Sinbad.
The film had a happy ending.
I'd rather read the book than watch the film.

dialogue.t: Have you read this adventure story?
Yes! I'd rather read the book than watch the film.
Why?
When I read, I use my imagination.
I prefer films to books. I like pictures.
Then you should try comics!

grammar.title: Giving reasons for preferences
grammar.ar: بعد أن نقول ما نفضّله نذكر السبب بـ because، أو نقارن بين الشيئين: I prefer books to films because I can use my imagination.
examples: I prefer comics to long books because they have pictures.
I'd rather read the book than watch the film.
I find films more exciting than books.

words.ex: We took the metro to the city centre.
There's often a traffic jam in the morning.
The park is close, so we go on foot.
The new bus seats are very comfortable.
You can buy a metro ticket with a bank card.
I'd prefer to walk. It's a nice day.

dialogue.t: Shall we ask Dad to drive us to the museum?
I'd rather take the metro. There's always a traffic jam.
Is the metro comfortable?
Very! It's cool and clean.
Is the museum near the station?
Yes, it's ten minutes on foot.
OK, but I'd prefer to come back by car!

grammar.title: Comparing choices
grammar.ar: نقارن بين خيارين بالمقارنة (quicker, more comfortable)، ثم نقول ما نفضّله: The metro is quicker than the car, so I'd rather take the metro.
examples: The metro is quicker than the bus.
I'd rather walk than wait for the bus.
I prefer going by car to going by bus.

words.ex: There are three options for the trip.
I suggest the science centre.
I prefer farms to zoos.
I don't mind. Both options are fine.
We had a vote, and the farm won.
Most of us want to go to the farm.

dialogue.t: We have three options: a farm, a science centre or a water park.
I suggest the science centre.
I'd rather go to the water park. It's more fun!
But we went there last year.
What about the farm?
I don't mind the farm. Let's have a vote.
Fifteen for the farm! Most of us prefer the farm.

grammar.title: Choosing together
grammar.ar: نقترح بـ I suggest …، ونقول ما نفضّله بـ I'd rather / I prefer، وإذا كان الخياران مناسبين نقول I don't mind. ونصف رأي المجموعة بـ Most of us …
examples: I suggest the farm.
I'd rather go to the science centre.
I don't mind. Both options are good.

words.ex: We were eating dinner when the doorbell rang.
Grandma's visit was a big surprise.
The kitchen was in a mess after the party.
We got ready very quickly.
Our guests arrived at seven.
We gave our guests coffee and dates.

dialogue.t: You look tired. What happened last night?
I was doing my homework when the doorbell rang.
Who was it?
My aunt and her children! It was a big surprise.
Was your house ready for guests?
No! The living room was in a mess, and my brothers were playing video games.

grammar.title: Past continuous: was / were + -ing
grammar.ar: نستخدم الماضي المستمر لحدث كان مستمراً في وقت معيّن في الماضي: I was doing my homework at 8 pm. ونستخدم when + الماضي البسيط للحدث القصير الذي حدث في أثنائه.
examples: I was doing my homework when the doorbell rang.
My brothers were playing video games.
What were you doing at eight o'clock?

words.ex: It rained heavily all night.
There was thunder and lightning last night.
We didn't take umbrellas, so we got wet.
There was a power cut, and the lights went off.
Suddenly, the sky went dark.
While we were walking home, it started to rain.

dialogue.t: Did you enjoy the picnic, Emma?
No! We were having lunch when suddenly it started to rain.
Did you get wet?
Very wet! It was raining heavily.
Was there thunder and lightning?
Yes! And while we were changing our clothes, there was a power cut!

grammar.title: when and while
grammar.ar: نستخدم while مع الحدث الطويل (الماضي المستمر)، ونستخدم when مع الحدث القصير (الماضي البسيط): While we were walking, it started to rain. / We were walking when it started to rain.
examples: While we were having lunch, it started to rain.
We were walking home when we heard thunder.
Suddenly, the lights went off.

words.ex: My cousin fell off his scooter.
I slipped on the wet floor.
She hurt her arm playing basketball.
His knee was bleeding a little.
Mum put a plaster on my finger.
Are you OK? Let me help you.

dialogue.t: What happened to your knee, Saad?
I fell off my bike in the park.
What were you doing?
I was riding down a hill when my wheel slipped.
Did you hurt yourself badly?
Not really. A man cleaned my knee and put a plaster on it.

grammar.title: Past continuous + when + past simple
grammar.ar: الماضي المستمر يصف ما كان يحدث، والماضي البسيط بعد when يصف الحدث المفاجئ الذي قطعه: I was riding my bike when I fell off.
examples: I was riding my bike when I fell off.
She was running when she slipped.
What were you doing when it happened?

words.ex: He dropped his phone on the floor.
I was looking for my keys all morning.
I didn't notice the rain.
The security guard helped the lost boy.
Mum was worried because I was late.
Luckily, someone found my bag.

dialogue.t: Did you buy new clothes for Eid?
Yes, but while I was trying on shoes, I dropped my purse.
Oh no! Were you worried?
Very! We went back to the shop, but it wasn't there.
What did you do?
We asked a security guard. Luckily, a woman found it.

grammar.title: while + past continuous
grammar.ar: نستخدم while + الماضي المستمر لنصف ما كنا نفعله، ثم الماضي البسيط لما حدث فجأة: While I was shopping, I dropped my purse.
examples: While I was trying on shoes, I dropped my purse.
I was looking for my bag when I saw the guard.
Luckily, someone found it.

words.ex: I took my brother's bag by mistake.
We laughed at the funny film.
I was embarrassed when I fell in front of everyone.
My uncle tells great jokes.
The lights went off in the middle of the film.
Grandpa fell asleep in front of the TV.

dialogue.t: Why was everyone laughing about the play?
We were doing the play when Khalid fell asleep on the stage!
In the middle of the play?
Yes! Then he woke up and said the wrong line by mistake.
Was he embarrassed?
At first, but then he laughed too.

grammar.title: Telling a funny story
grammar.ar: نبدأ بالخلفية بالماضي المستمر (We were …ing)، ثم نذكر الحدث المضحك بالماضي البسيط، ثم نقول كيف كانت ردة فعل الناس.
examples: We were sitting in class when a bird flew in.
Everyone laughed.
I felt embarrassed, but then I laughed too.

words.ex: One day, a boy found a box in the sand.
At first, I was scared, but then I felt OK.
We stayed inside because of the sandstorm.
We got lost in the old part of the city.
Luckily, the shop was still open.
In the end, we found the way home.

dialogue.t: Grandpa, tell me a story!
One day, I was looking after our camels in the desert.
I was sitting under a tree when suddenly a sandstorm started.
What did you do?
I got lost. Luckily, the camels knew the way home.
And in the end?
In the end, I got home at night.

grammar.title: Story words
grammar.ar: نرتّب القصة بكلمات: One day (البداية) – At first – Suddenly (حدث مفاجئ) – Luckily (شيء جيد حدث) – In the end (النهاية). والخلفية بالماضي المستمر والأحداث بالماضي البسيط.
examples: One day, I was walking in the desert.
Suddenly, a sandstorm started.
In the end, I got home safely.

words.ex: Let's check the weather forecast before the trip.
It'll probably rain later.
Take a jacket. It might be cold.
Close the windows. A dust storm is coming.
The temperature will reach 40 degrees.
It's cloudy, but it isn't raining.

dialogue.t: What does the weather forecast say for Friday?
It will be sunny, but it might be windy in the afternoon.
Will there be a dust storm?
Probably not. It'll be cloudy in the afternoon.
What about the temperature?
About 28 degrees. Perfect for a picnic!

grammar.title: will / won't / might
grammar.ar: نستخدم will للتوقّع عندما نكون متأكدين تقريباً، وwon't (= will not) للنفي، وmight عندما لا نكون متأكدين: It might rain. وبعدها كلها الفعل في صيغته الأساسية.
examples: It will be sunny tomorrow.
It won't rain this week.
It might be windy in the afternoon.

words.ex: In the future, cars will drive themselves.
Robots will definitely help us at home.
A robot cleaned the floor.
I don't think we'll use paper money in the future.
Some cities are testing driverless cars.
Astronauts live and work in space.

dialogue.t: We need predictions about life in 2050.
I think everyone will have a robot at home.
Definitely! And people will probably travel in driverless cars.
Flying taxis might be normal in the future.
Will people go on holiday in space?
They might, but it'll be very expensive.

grammar.title: Predictions: how sure are you?
grammar.ar: متأكد 100%: will definitely. متأكد غالباً: will probably. غير متأكد: might. غالباً لا: probably won't / I don't think … will. لاحظ أن definitely وprobably تأتيان بعد will وقبل won't.
examples: People will definitely use robots.
We'll probably travel in driverless cars.
I don't think schools will disappear.

words.ex: I promise I'll call you tonight.
I won't be late again.
Dad always keeps his promises.
The bus arrived on time.
Please tidy up your toys.
You can trust me.

dialogue.t: Mum, can I go to Ziyad's house tomorrow?
What about your homework?
I promise I'll finish my homework first.
Last time, you didn't keep your promise.
I won't forget this time. You can trust me.
OK. But be home on time.
I won't be late, I promise.

grammar.title: Promises: I'll / I won't
grammar.ar: نستخدم will للوعد: I promise I'll help. وwon't = will not: I won't be late. ويمكن أن نضع I promise في أول الجملة أو في آخرها.
examples: I promise I'll tidy up my room.
